body:
## Problem and resulting behavior

#5095's new owned manifest mode removes legacy revision rescans, but its explicit publication setup remains allocation-heavy: at exactb57, five matched128/512 groups allocate27.53/27.22 times standalone setup and13.14/6.26 times setup+GC. All original failed/noisy results are retained at https://github.com/snissn/gomap/issues/5095#issuecomment-6039166101. The diagnostic wholefixture profile attributes67.26MB to encodeIndexPage; this is sampled attribution, not exclusive GC or an exact savings promise.

The current production candidate owns a fresh4096-byte image per allocator index page. Use a detached immutable encoding description bound to the same frozen pageID/depth/checksum, rendered into caller-owned storage through existing opaque candidate views. The generic sink retains owning isolation. This changes candidate representation, not on-disk format, page identity, retirement authority or real COW page counts.

## Deliverable and dependencies

Primary deliverable: PR implementation supporting #5095, allowed to land atomically in that PR. Acceptance owner: #5090 coordinator. Predecessors: accepted #5091 decision, landed #5101 harness and exact #5095 b57 format/publication contract snapshot. #5095 remains provisional and unaccepted pending this slice and its remaining cost/noise/foreground/rollout gates. Parent #5090 full H/E remains required.

This adopts only allocator candidate index-image representation. Existing #5044/#4877/#4878 and externally owned PRs remain separately owned and open. No broader roadmap takeover.

## Architectural contract

- Keep both visible/seal generations, queued prefixes, rollback forks, durable slots, held-root pins, exact metadata reservations and resource-sync -> index-sync -> meta-sync -> prefix-consumption ordering.
- Caller-destination encoder clears and encodes all4096 bytes identically, including reserved bytes and CRC.
- At production Prepare use one admitted transaction-owned scratch, never retain its mutable bytes in a page view. Record finite description/table capacity before allocation; non-index eager images remain charged. Do not claim local scratch is stack-owned without evidence.
- The detached canonical header/child-description plan remains immutable after future candidates, fork/materialization, abort, release or mutation of a caller's CopyTo destination.
- Len/CopyTo/Pages preserve existing output semantics. Generic AppendPageSink owns independent bytes; CandidatePageWriter may retain views indefinitely.
- Production pager bridge populates under the existing Pager.Write mutex/copy contract. No unlocked page population, global pool/cache, alternative authority plane, WAL/checksum shortcut or admission-cap increase.
- Include actual second-pass encoding/CRC work, descriptions, scratch, both generations and debt retention in the ledger. Removing heap images does not erase physical COW or grant performance acceptance.

## Validation and evidence

- [ ] Byte-for-byte eager/description equivalence for empty/sparse/multichunk/reused metadata and exact checksum/order/IDs.
- [ ] Retaining and mutating generic sinks; retained views after fork/abort/release/later materialization/destination mutation.
- [ ] Existing candidate prefix, rollback, dual-slot/held-root/recovery and affected race tests pass at exactsource; source-bound complete working bytes retained before semantic checks.
- [ ] Independent source review accepts ownership/admission/lifetime and simplification before expensive comparison.
- [ ] Exact source/compiled inputs/toolchain/binary freeze; same wholefixture diagnostic reports setupbytes, description capacity, actual encodingpasses/COWpages and debt/highwater. Previous failures retained.
- [ ] #5095 unchanged public wholeGC/foreground/noise/rollout gates remain required. A remaining >100MB setup residual requires further evidence/alternatives and explicit necessary-residual decision; this ticket alone cannot satisfy them.

Conditional onechunk/R=1 shape yields15 index pages and18 pages per generation; two generations across512 explicit revisions imply60MiB index image backing. The original node-backed <=64B description is rejected because an indefinitely retained view could hold an entire allocator subtree. Its exact source packet remains retained. The selected correction owns a detached576-byte canonical header/child descriptor plan only for actual index pages, with no tree/chunk/generation references. Source-derived candidate representation is40P+576I+4096(P-I), plus separately charged4096-byte preparation scratch and all existing state/reservation/ID capacities. Verify compiler/unsafe-size behavior; the empty-case transient increase remains reported. This is a bound to verify, not a forecast or replacement target. Compressed-prefix allocator format is the deeper physical-work alternative and requires its own format/refusal/graph decision.

Source baseline b57e9622f80fae29527aac6bd538284abceb649e. Inquiry notes/L-publication-architecture-inquiry-v2.md SHA fac20492a991e1d9fd4cff0d991638f5ec18806379b9ea2645534752f10f8718. No runtime or parent performance acceptance. Reviewed current-head CI and mature hosted review apply before merge.
title: [R1 architecture] Encode allocator candidate index pages from frozen descriptions
